data.text:
hey vibecoders,  

what do you hate about building with Claude code? 
 
- frontend 
- cost of claude code 
- fable (disabled) 
- compacting...
- waiting for Claude’s response

choose ONE

GPT-5.6のリークまとめ動画が来ていた。

観ていて思ったのは、Fable 5と同じような執拗さを感じたこと。

Minecraftでは地下まで作るし、Voxelアートでも詳細な部分や動きや光りにも拘っている。こういうこだわりと執拗さは、Fable 5で見られたものに近いのではないだろうか。

ただし、Fable 5に追いつけるかは不明だ。理由は二つある。

一つは、ハーネスの問題。Fable 5にはClaude Codeという、馬鹿みたいに機能がゴテゴテしたハーネスがあり、Fable 5はそれを華麗に使いこなしていた。対して、GPT-5.6が使うCodexは、ハーネスとしてとてもシンプルだ。
（というか、今回のリークはチャットのものなので、ツール利用などの能力は不明）

二つ目はキャラクターであり、この部分はFable 5というか、Anthropicが明らかに先行している。つい最近の中の人のインタビューでも言われていたが、Fable 5／Mythosでは「強強エンジニアの仕事を学習させていた」疑惑がある。
また、ユーザーに「察してくれると思わせる」ような対話能力は特別だ。GPTモデルでそれを可能にするのは難しいだろう。というか、OpenAIはそういうものを求めていない気もする。

---

総じて、私はとても楽しみなのだが、心配はコストだ。

単純にトークンの値段が上がるだけではなく、「GPT-5.6 Proでなければ性能を発揮しない」ということも想定されるからだ。GPTのProモデルは、伝統的に桁違いに高額だ。

data.text:
fablemania 

today in the park my heart stopped when i found out you could pick fable in claude code im a fucking addict i dropped the book frantically typed a prompt already running through how im gonna dump all my problems into a skill and live perfectly aaaand turns out the option was there the message sent but i got back a plain 500 error and fable still wasnt available

GLM is ahead in terms of physics, for pure design (3d Tasks) GPT should be better considering the training data OpenAI uses.

I have been coding a majority of my full stack app [that is in production, and has a multi million euro ARR, so the stakes are high] on my own with Claude in multiple systems (claude code, Cursor, VS Code...) I have used Opus ever since September last year as my go to model for programming. Last week since it came out I started GLM 5.2 and I have to say: I built more features in a week than I did in a month with Opus 4.7 ... The crazy thing is that neither me nor my team had any issues with features we made with GLM which is a massive step up from Opus (but we were even more impressed and faster with Fable).
For now while Fable is not available, we'll be using GLM and even with Fable being available again we've found some uses for GLM that it excells at and beats gpt and claude / grok by miles in: the fine tuning of agents.
First time an AI model managed to write systeminstructions that I did not need to review a million times. First time a Model chose the right AI settings for tasks without me needing to intervene all the time. I created sophisticated subagents and skills so claude would do an alright job at it, but GLM, even without my harness, built things better than claude did with it.

For instance: classic rag will not do a great job for my type of use cases. I built on existing graph rag architectures added custom features and lots of complicated domain specific logics to get my AI systems to have better results than any of the competition.
For half a year I have now been working on a completely new retrival logic, trained custom embedding models for it, basically created a new type of rag, can't tell too much about it yet.
I let GLM work on it in a new branch, it gave insane suggestions we had not considered yet, also no other model did, idk how... and it implemented them in such a simple but yet brilliant way, upped our own benchmarks by 13% which is insane.

So all I can say: give GLM a try, you won't fucking regret it. Especially if you put it in the cursor harness, worked better than claude code.

the real move wasn't finding the next best model on the leaderboard. it was asking: what were we actually buying by routing everything through a single oracle?

turns out, something structurally better exists.

a panel of models with role diversity (security architect, skeptical economist, systems historian) plus a frontier judge synthesizing their disagreements scored 69.0% on DRACO deep research benchmarks. fable 5 solo scored 65.3%. the budget panel (gemini 3 flash, kimi k2.6, deepseek v4 pro) scored 64.7% at 40% of the cost.

the insight buried in those numbers: the architecture of deliberation outperforms the intelligence of any individual voice. management figured this out decades ago (committees, red teams, peer review). ai development spent 5 years chasing smarter single models without asking whether 3 medium-capable systems forced into structured disagreement might outperform 1 exceptional one uncontested.

turns out they might.

the perspective council stacks model diversity and role diversity at the same time. each panelist gets a different expert persona. the judge reads all responses, notes agreements and contradictions, synthesizes from the pattern. slower than a sprint. generally more right.

i build and ship daily. Claude Code, Codex, whatever ships fastest. SaaS, tools, automations. ⭐ if AI can build it, i've probably broken it first. what works → link in bio

Now that Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 are gone…

I believe Web scraping will never be the same.

(100% open-source visual search at scale)

PixelRAG is a retrieval system that skips HTML parsing completely.

Instead of scraping a page into text and embedding chunks, it screenshots the page and retrieves the image. A vision-language model reads the answer straight off the pixels.

Why that matters: parsing is where web RAG quietly loses information.

- A single HTML-to-text parser can drop 40%+ of a page.
- Tables, charts, and layout get flattened or thrown out.
- Swapping parsers alone can move accuracy ~10 points on the same docs.

PixelRAG indexes the page a person actually sees. The team built a visual index of all of Wikipedia, 30M+ screenshots, and it still beats the strongest text RAG baseline by 18.1% on text-only QA.

The repo also ships a Claude Code plugin that gives Claude eyes.

It lets Claude screenshot any URL and read the rendered page instead of scraping the DOM. So you can hand it a live page, an arXiv paper, or your local site and ask what it actually looks like.

One setup script. No MCP server, no backend.

How the pipeline works:

- Renders each document (web, PDF, image) to image tiles.
- Embeds them with Qwen3-VL-Embedding, LoRA fine-tuned on screenshots.
- Builds a FAISS index and serves a search API.

A stronger reader model lifts accuracy with no re-indexing, since the index is just pixels.

Everything is open-source under Apache-2.0.

GitHub repo: https://t.co/qtFPhQ9zxv…

There has been a lot of hype around GLM 5.2 this week.

Most of it is deserved. Some of it is not.

Here is the honest breakdown what it actually is, and exactly how to use it for free.

GLM-5.2 was built by Zhipu AI, now called Z .ai, a company spun out of Tsinghua University in China. It launched June 13, 2026. The open weights went public on Hugging Face June 16-17.

Start with the claim that matters most.

According to Artificial Analysis, an independent AI research firm, GLM-5.2 is currently the #1 open-weights AI model in the world and 4th best overall, behind only a couple of OpenAI and Anthropic models.

That part of the hype is real. And unlike the models ahead of it, you can download this one and run it yourself. For free. With no licensing fees, ever.

Here is what genuinely deserves the attention.

MIT licensed with no regional restrictions. Self-host it, fine-tune it, deploy it commercially, zero limitations. A truly usable 1 million token context window, one of the largest of any open model. Two reasoning modes, High and Max. And cloud API pricing roughly 10x cheaper than Claude or GPT-5.

Now here is how to actually use it for free three ways, easiest to most technical.

Method 1: Z .ai directly. Go to z .ai. GLM-5.2 powers the chat interface. Start using it in your browser immediately. No install, no setup. The fastest way to test it. One warning server congestion at launch caused timeouts for a lot of users. If it is slow, wait a day or use the next method.

Method 2: OpenRouter. If you do not want to route data through Z .ai's servers, OpenRouter hosts GLM-5.2 through third-party providers. Sign up, get an API key, and use the low-cost or free-tier access. Best option for developers who want API access without the data routing concern.

Method 3: Self-host the weights. The weights are on Hugging Face under MIT license. Download, run on your own hardware, and your data never leaves your machine. The catch: it is a large model roughly 744B total parameters, around 40B active. You realistically need serious GPU hardware, around 8x H100 80GB or equivalent. Not a laptop job. But for enterprises, fully private deployment costs nothing in licensing.

It also works as a drop-in Claude Code replacement, plugs into Claude Code, Cline, OpenCode, Goose, and other OpenAI-compatible CLIs by overriding the base URL and model name.

Now here is the part of the hype that is not deserved, the honest caveats.

GLM-5.2 is not the single best AI model in the world. Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 still score higher overall. Anyone telling you it beats every model is overselling it.

It is text-only. For images or video in the GLM family, you need GLM-4.6V.

And there is real context behind the launch. Zhipu released GLM-5.2 as a direct response to US export controls, specifically the directive that forced Anthropic to block foreign access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models within 48 hours. The founder framed it as a stance: "the path to AGI must never be enclosed by high walls."

If you use the cloud API, you are routing data through servers operated by a Chinese company. For anything sensitive, self-hosting is the right path. Know that before you wire it into something important.

Here is the honest bottom line.

GLM-5.2 is not the best model on the planet. But it is the best one you can download, run privately, and use commercially for free with a 1 million token context window, at the exact moment the most powerful Western models are being locked behind export controls.

The hype overshoots on "best model ever."

It undersells on "free frontier intelligence you actually own."

The second one is the real story.

Source: Zhipu AI / Z .ai · Artificial Analysis · Pandaily · SuperCareer · June 13-17, 2026

Not “good for the price.”
Not “interesting because it is open.”
Just good.

Why I keep using it:

The context window matters because agent work is not a single prompt. It is repo state, design constraints, existing components, logs, tests, product requirements, and iteration history.

The design part is the surprise.

- #1 on Design Arena website
- #1 on code categories
- #4 on UI components
- #4 on agent webapps
- #2 in Code Arena Frontend, behind Fable 5

It is not just writing React.

It is better at the first visual pass: layout, spacing, hierarchy, landing pages, dashboards, settings screens.

How to run it:

1. ZAI API
$1.40 / 1M input
$0.26 / 1M cached input
$4.40 / 1M output

2. ZAI Coding Plan
Starts at $18/mo
Works through tools like Claude Code, Cline, OpenCode

3. Fireworks / managed inference
Fireworks runs GLM-5.2 serverless at roughly the same pricing.

Best path if you want API access without hosting a 743B model.

Cheapest routes I found:
~$1.20 input
~$4.10 output
per 1M tokens

Unsloth GGUF:

1-bit: ~217–229GB
2-bit: ~239GB, about 245GB memory needed
4-bit: ~436–467GB
8-bit: ~801–820GB
BF16: ~1.5TB

My routing:

Use GLM-5.2 for large-context coding and frontend/design generation.

Use managed inference for real work.

Use local only when control, privacy, or resilience matters enough to justify the hardware.
